stories.title: What Soaring Treasury Yields Mean for the Economy
stories.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield jumped to a 19-year high. Higher yields raise borrowing costs across the economy, from mortgages to corporate loans. CNBC looked at what the spike means for growth and markets.
stories.whyItMatters: Rising yields ripple into mortgage rates, corporate borrowing costs, and stock valuations, touching nearly every portfolio.
whatToWatch: Further moves in the 10-year Treasury yield
Any Fed response to the yield spike
Effects on mortgage rates and corporate borrowing
questions: What is driving the spike in yields right now?
How long can yields stay this elevated before growth slows?

stories.title: 10-Year Treasury and Japanese Government Bond Yields Hit Multi-Decade Highs
stories.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield and Japanese government bond yields both climbed to their highest levels in decades on the same day. CNBC called it a historic day for global bond markets.
stories.whyItMatters: Simultaneous multi-decade highs in the world's two largest bond markets signal a broad, global repricing of borrowing costs.

Any policy response from the Fed or Bank of Japan
questions: What common factor is pushing US and Japanese yields higher at the same time?

stories.title: Market Breadth Narrows to Levels Not Seen Since the Dot-Com Peak
stories.summary: A shrinking number of stocks are driving overall market gains, according to MarketWatch. The last time breadth was this narrow was at the dot-com peak.
stories.whyItMatters: Narrow leadership means the market's gains rest on fewer companies, a pattern that has preceded past downturns.

stories.title: Traders Now See Next Fed Move as an October Rate Hike
stories.summary: Markets are now pricing in a Fed interest rate hike in October, CNBC reported. The shift follows comments from Fed official Barr and a hotter-than-expected inflation reading.
stories.whyItMatters: A pivot toward a rate hike, rather than a cut, would mark a shift in the Fed's path and could hit stock and bond prices.
whatToWatch: Upcoming inflation data ahead of that meeting
Any further comments from Fed officials, including Barr
questions: How hot was the inflation reading that shifted expectations?

stories.title: Does Gridlock in Washington Actually Help Stocks? What the Data Shows
stories.summary: MarketWatch examined historical market data to test the idea that political gridlock in Washington is good for stocks. The piece weighs the theory against past market performance.
stories.whyItMatters: Investors often assume gridlock reduces policy risk for markets, so the historical record matters for how much weight to give that assumption.
questions: Does the historical pattern actually hold up, or is it coincidence?
